verses.first: In Judah is God known;
verses.second: his Name is great in Israel.

verses.first: At Salem is his tabernacle,
verses.second: and his dwelling is in Zion.

verses.first: There he broke the flashing arrows,
verses.second: the shield, the sword, and the weapons of battle.

verses.first: How glorious you are!
verses.second: more splendid than the everlasting mountains!

verses.first: The strong of heart have been despoiled; they sink into sleep;
verses.second: none of the warriors can lift a hand.

verses.first: At your rebuke, O God of Jacob,
verses.second: both horse and rider lie stunned.

verses.first: What terror you inspire!
verses.second: who can stand before you when you are angry?

verses.first: From heaven you pronounced judgment;
verses.second: the earth was afraid and was still;

verses.first: When God rose up to judgment
verses.second: and to save all the oppressed of the earth.

verses.first: Truly, wrathful Edom will give you thanks,
verses.second: and the remnant of Hamath will keep your feasts.

verses.first: Make a vow to the Lord your God and keep it;
verses.second: let all around him bring gifts to him who is worthy to be feared.

verses.first: He breaks the spirit of princes,
verses.second: and strikes terror in the kings of the earth.

verses.first: I will cry aloud to God;
verses.second: I will cry aloud, and he will hear me.

verses.first: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord;
verses.second: my hands were stretched out by night and did not tire; I refused to be comforted.

verses.first: I think of God, I am restless,
verses.second: I ponder, and my spirit faints.

verses.first: You will not let my eyelids close;
verses.second: I am troubled and I cannot speak.

verses.first: I consider the days of old;
verses.second: I remember the years long past;

verses.first: I commune with my heart in the night;
verses.second: I ponder and search my mind.

verses.first: Will the Lord cast me off for ever?
verses.second: will he no more show his favor?

verses.first: Has his loving-kindness come to an end for ever?
verses.second: has his promise failed for evermore?

verses.first: Has God forgotten to be gracious?
verses.second: has he, in his anger, withheld his compassion?

verses.first: And I said, “My grief is this:
verses.second: the right hand of the Most High has lost its power.”

verses.first: I will remember the works of the Lord,
verses.second: and call to mind your wonders of old time.

verses.first: I will meditate on all your acts
verses.second: and ponder your mighty deeds.

verses.first: Your way, O God, is holy;
verses.second: who is so great a god as our God?

verses.first: You are the God who works wonders
verses.second: and have declared your power among the peoples.

verses.first: By your strength you have redeemed your people,
verses.second: the children of Jacob and Joseph.

verses.first: The waters saw you, O God; the waters saw you and trembled;
verses.second: the very depths were shaken.

verses.first: The clouds poured out water; the skies thundered;
verses.second: your arrows flashed to and fro;

verses.first: The sound of your thunder was in the whirlwind; your lightnings lit up the world;
verses.second: the earth trembled and shook.

verses.first: Your way was in the sea, and your paths in the great waters,
verses.second: yet your footsteps were not seen.

verses.first: You led your people like a flock
verses.second: by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

verses.first: Hear my teaching, O my people;
verses.second: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

verses.first: I will open my mouth in a parable;
verses.second: I will declare the mysteries of ancient times.

verses.first: That which we have heard and known, and what our forefathers have told us,
verses.second: we will not hide from their children.

verses.first: We will recount to generations to come the praiseworthy deeds and the power of the Lord,
verses.second: and the wonderful works he has done.

verses.first: He gave his decrees to Jacob and established a law for Israel,
verses.second: which he commanded them to teach their children;

verses.first: That the generations to come might know, and the children yet unborn;
verses.second: that they in their turn might tell it to their children;

verses.first: So that they might put their trust in God,
verses.second: and not forget the deeds of God, but keep his commandments;

verses.first: And not be like their forefathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation,
verses.second: a generation whose heart was not steadfast, and whose spirit was not faithful to God.

verses.first: The people of Ephraim, armed with the bow,
verses.second: turned back in the day of battle;

verses.first: They did not keep the covenant of God,
verses.second: and refused to walk in his law;

verses.first: They forgot what he had done,
verses.second: and the wonders he had shown them.

verses.first: He worked marvels in the sight of their forefathers,
verses.second: in the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan.

verses.first: He split open the sea and let them pass through;
verses.second: he made the waters stand up like walls.

verses.first: He led them with a cloud by day,
verses.second: and all the night through with a glow of fire.

verses.first: He split the hard rocks in the wilderness
verses.second: and gave them drink as from the great deep.

verses.first: He brought streams out of the cliff,
verses.second: and the waters gushed out like rivers.

verses.first: But they went on sinning against him,
verses.second: rebelling in the desert against the Most High.

verses.first: They tested God in their hearts,
verses.second: demanding food for their craving.

verses.first: They railed against God and said,
verses.second: “Can God set a table in the wilderness?

verses.first: True, he struck the rock, the waters gushed out, and the gullies overflowed;
verses.second: but is he able to give bread or to provide meat for his people?”

verses.first: When the Lord heard this, he was full of wrath;
verses.second: a fire was kindled against Jacob, and his anger mounted against Israel;

verses.first: For they had no faith in God,
verses.second: nor did they put their trust in his saving power.

verses.first: So he commanded the clouds above
verses.second: and opened the doors of heaven.

verses.first: He rained down manna upon them to eat
verses.second: and gave them grain from heaven.

verses.first: So mortals ate the bread of angels;
verses.second: he provided for them food enough.

verses.first: He caused the east wind to blow in the heavens
verses.second: and led out the south wind by his might.

verses.first: He rained down flesh upon them like dust
verses.second: and wingèd birds like the sand of the sea.

verses.first: He let it fall in the midst of their camp
verses.second: and round about their dwellings.

verses.first: So they ate and were well filled,
verses.second: for he gave them what they craved.

verses.first: But they did not stop their craving,
verses.second: though the food was still in their mouths.

verses.first: So God’s anger mounted against them;
verses.second: he slew their strongest men and laid low the youth of Israel.

verses.first: In spite of all this, they went on sinning
verses.second: and had no faith in his wonderful works.

verses.first: So he brought their days to an end like a breath
verses.second: and their years in sudden terror.

verses.first: Whenever he slew them, they would seek him,
verses.second: and repent, and diligently search for God.

verses.first: They would remember that God was their rock,
verses.second: and the Most High God their redeemer.

verses.first: But they flattered him with their mouths
verses.second: and lied to him with their tongues.

verses.first: Their heart was not steadfast toward him,
verses.second: and they were not faithful to his covenant.

verses.first: But he was so merciful that he forgave their sins and did not destroy them;
verses.second: many times he held back his anger and did not permit his wrath to be roused.

verses.first: For he remembered that they were but flesh,
verses.second: a breath that goes forth and does not return.

verses.first: How often the people disobeyed him in the wilderness
verses.second: and offended him in the desert!

verses.first: Again and again they tempted God
verses.second: and provoked the Holy One of Israel.

verses.first: They did not remember his power
verses.second: in the day when he ransomed them from the enemy;

verses.first: How he wrought his signs in Egypt
verses.second: and his omens in the field of Zoan.

verses.first: He turned their rivers into blood,
verses.second: so that they could not drink of their streams.

verses.first: He sent swarms of flies among them, which ate them up,
verses.second: and frogs, which destroyed them.

verses.first: He gave their crops to the caterpillar,
verses.second: the fruit of their toil to the locust.

verses.first: He killed their vines with hail
verses.second: and their sycamores with frost.

verses.first: He delivered their cattle to hailstones
verses.second: and their livestock to hot thunderbolts.

verses.first: He poured out upon them his blazing anger:
verses.second: fury, indignation, and distress, a troop of destroying angels. `

verses.first: He gave full rein to his anger; he did not spare their souls from death;
verses.second: but delivered their lives to the plague.

verses.first: He struck down all the firstborn of Egypt,
verses.second: the flower of manhood in the dwellings of Ham.

verses.first: He led out his people like sheep
verses.second: and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.

verses.first: He led them to safety, and they were not afraid;
verses.second: but the sea overwhelmed their enemies.

verses.first: He brought them to his holy land,
verses.second: the mountain his right hand had won.

verses.first: He drove out the Canaanites before them and apportioned an inheritance to them by lot;
verses.second: he made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.

verses.first: But they tested the Most High God, and defied him,
verses.second: and did not keep his commandments.

verses.first: They turned away and were disloyal like their fathers;
verses.second: they were undependable like a warped bow.

verses.first: They grieved him with their hill-altars
verses.second: and provoked his displeasure with their idols.

verses.first: When God heard this, he was angry
verses.second: and utterly rejected Israel.

verses.first: He forsook the shrine at Shiloh,
verses.second: the tabernacle where he had lived among his people.

verses.first: He delivered the ark into captivity,
verses.second: his glory into the adversary’s hand.

verses.first: He gave his people to the sword
verses.second: and was angered against his inheritance.

verses.first: The fire consumed their young men;
verses.second: there were no wedding songs for their maidens.

verses.first: Their priests fell by the sword,
verses.second: and their widows made no lamentation.

verses.first: Then the Lord woke as though from sleep,
verses.second: like a warrior refreshed with wine.

verses.first: He struck his enemies on the backside
verses.second: and put them to perpetual shame.

verses.first: He rejected the tent of Joseph
verses.second: and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim;

verses.first: He chose instead the tribe of Judah
verses.second: and Mount Zion, which he loved.

verses.first: He built his sanctuary like the heights of heaven,
verses.second: like the earth which he founded for ever.

verses.first: He chose David his servant,
verses.second: and took him away from the sheepfolds.

verses.first: He brought him from following the ewes,
verses.second: to be a shepherd over Jacob his people and over Israel his inheritance.

verses.first: So he shepherded them with a faithful and true heart
verses.second: and guided them with the skillfulness of his hands.

verses.first: O God, the heathen have come into your inheritance; they have profaned your holy temple;
verses.second: they have made Jerusalem a heap of rubble.

verses.first: They have given the bodies of your servants as food for the birds of the air,
verses.second: and the flesh of your faithful ones to the beasts of the field.

verses.first: They have shed their blood like water on every side of Jerusalem,
verses.second: and there was no one to bury them.

verses.first: We have become a reproach to our neighbors,
verses.second: an object of scorn and derision to those around us.

verses.first: How long will you be angry, O Lord?
verses.second: will your fury blaze like fire for ever?

verses.first: Pour out your wrath upon the heathen who have not known you
verses.second: and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon your Name.

verses.first: For they have devoured Jacob
verses.second: and made his dwelling a ruin.

verses.first: Remember not our past sins; let your compassion be swift to meet us;
verses.second: for we have been brought very low.

verses.first: Help us, O God our Savior, for the glory of your Name;
verses.second: deliver us and forgive us our sins, for your Name’s sake.

verses.first: Why should the heathen say, “Where is their God?”
verses.second: Let it be known among the heathen and in our sight that you avenge the shedding of your servants’ blood.

verses.first: Let the sorrowful sighing of the prisoners come before you,
verses.second: and by your great might spare those who are condemned to die.

verses.first: May the revilings with which they reviled you, O Lord,
verses.second: return seven-fold into their bosoms.

verses.first: For we are your people and the sheep of your pasture;
verses.second: we will give you thanks for ever and show forth your praise from age to age.

verses.first: Hear, O Shepherd of Israel, leading Joseph like a flock;
verses.second: shine forth, you that are enthroned upon the cherubim.

verses.first: In the presence of Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh,
verses.second: stir up your strength and come to help us.

verses.first: Restore us, O God of hosts;
verses.second: show the light of your countenance, and we shall be saved.

verses.first: O Lord God of hosts,
verses.second: how long will you be angered despite the prayers of your people?

verses.first: You have fed them with the bread of tears;
verses.second: you have given them bowls of tears to drink.

verses.first: You have made us the derision of our neighbors,
verses.second: and our enemies laugh us to scorn.

verses.first: Restore us, O God of hosts;
verses.second: show the light of your countenance, and we shall be saved.

verses.first: You have brought a vine out of Egypt;
verses.second: you cast out the nations and planted it.

verses.first: You prepared the ground for it;
verses.second: it took root and filled the land.

verses.first: The mountains were covered by its shadow
verses.second: and the towering cedar trees by its boughs.

verses.first: You stretched out its tendrils to the Sea
verses.second: and its branches to the River.

verses.first: Why have you broken down its wall,
verses.second: so that all who pass by pluck off its grapes?

verses.first: The wild boar of the forest has ravaged it,
verses.second: and the beasts of the field have grazed upon it.

verses.first: Turn now, O God of hosts, look down from heaven; behold and tend this vine;
verses.second: preserve what your right hand has planted.

verses.first: They burn it with fire like rubbish;
verses.second: at the rebuke of your countenance let them perish.

verses.first: Let your hand be upon the man of your right hand,
verses.second: the son of man you have made so strong for yourself.

verses.first: And so will we never turn away from you;
verses.second: give us life, that we may call upon your Name.

verses.first: Restore us, O Lord God of hosts;
verses.second: show the light of your countenance, and we shall be saved.

verses.first: Sing with joy to God our strength
verses.second: and raise a loud shout to the God of Jacob.

verses.first: Raise a song and sound the timbrel,
verses.second: the merry harp, and the lyre.

verses.first: Blow the ram’s-horn at the new moon,
verses.second: and at the full moon, the day of our feast.

verses.first: For this is a statute for Israel,
verses.second: a law of the God of Jacob.

verses.first: He laid it as a solemn charge upon Joseph,
verses.second: when he came out of the land of Egypt.

verses.first: I heard an unfamiliar voice saying
verses.second: “I eased his shoulder from the burden; his hands were set free from bearing the load.”

verses.first: You called on me in trouble, and I saved you;
verses.second: I answered you from the secret place of thunder and tested you at the waters of Meribah.

verses.first: Hear, O my people, and I will admonish you:
verses.second: O Israel, if you would but listen to me!

verses.first: There shall be no strange god among you;
verses.second: you shall not worship a foreign god.

verses.first: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and said,
verses.second: “Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.”

verses.first: And yet my people did not hear my voice,
verses.second: and Israel would not obey me.

verses.first: So I gave them over to the stubbornness of their hearts,
verses.second: to follow their own devices.

verses.first: Oh, that my people would listen to me!
verses.second: that Israel would walk in my ways!

verses.first: I should soon subdue their enemies
verses.second: and turn my hand against their foes.

verses.first: Those who hate the Lord would cringe before him,
verses.second: and their punishment would last for ever.

verses.first: But Israel would I feed with the finest wheat
verses.second: and satisfy him with honey from the rock.

verses.first: God takes his stand in the council of heaven;
verses.second: he gives judgment in the midst of the gods:

verses.first: “How long will you judge unjustly,
verses.second: and show favor to the wicked?

verses.first: Save the weak and the orphan;
verses.second: defend the humble and needy;

verses.first: Rescue the weak and the poor;
verses.second: deliver them from the power of the wicked.

verses.first: They do not know, neither do they understand; they go about in darkness;
verses.second: all the foundations of the earth are shaken.

verses.first: Now I say to you, ‘You are gods,
verses.second: and all of you children of the Most High;

verses.first: Nevertheless, you shall die like mortals,
verses.second: and fall like any prince.’”

verses.first: Arise, O God, and rule the earth,
verses.second: for you shall take all nations for your own.

verses.first: O God, do not be silent;
verses.second: do not keep still nor hold your peace, O God;

verses.first: For your enemies are in tumult,
verses.second: and those who hate you have lifted up their heads.

verses.first: They take secret counsel against your people
verses.second: and plot against those whom you protect.

verses.first: They have said, “Come, let us wipe them out from among the nations;
verses.second: let the name of Israel be remembered no more.”

verses.first: They have conspired together;
verses.second: they have made an alliance against you:

verses.first: The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites;
verses.second: the Moabites and the Hagarenes;

verses.first: Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek;
verses.second: the Philistines and those who dwell in Tyre.

verses.first: The Assyrians also have joined them,
verses.second: and have come to help the people of Lot.

verses.first: Do to them as you did to Midian,
verses.second: to Sisera, and to Jabin at the river of Kishon:

verses.first: They were destroyed at Endor;
verses.second: they became like dung upon the ground.

verses.first: Make their leaders like Oreb and Zeëb,
verses.second: and all their commanders like Zebah and Zalmunna,

verses.first: Who said, “Let us take for ourselves
verses.second: the fields of God as our possession.”

verses.first: O my God, make them like whirling dust
verses.second: and like chaff before the wind;

verses.first: Like fire that burns down a forest,
verses.second: like the flame that sets mountains ablaze.

verses.first: Drive them with your tempest
verses.second: and terrify them with your storm;

verses.first: Cover their faces with shame, O Lord,
verses.second: that they may seek your Name.

verses.first: Let them be disgraced and terrified for ever;
verses.second: let them be put to confusion and perish.

verses.first: Let them know that you, whose Name is Yahweh,
verses.second: you alone are the Most High over all the earth.

verses.first: How dear to me is your dwelling, O Lord of hosts!
verses.second: My soul has a desire and longing for the courts of the Lord; my heart and my flesh rejoice in the living God.

verses.first: The sparrow has found her a house and the swallow a nest where she may lay her young;
verses.second: by the side of your altars, O Lord of hosts, my King and my God.

verses.first: Happy are they who dwell in your house!
verses.second: they will always be praising you.

verses.first: Happy are the people whose strength is in you!
verses.second: whose hearts are set on the pilgrims’ way.

verses.first: Those who go through the desolate valley will find it a place of springs,
verses.second: for the early rains have covered it with pools of water.

verses.first: They will climb from height to height,
verses.second: and the God of gods will reveal himself in Zion.

verses.first: Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer;
verses.second: hearken, O God of Jacob.

verses.first: Behold our defender, O God;
verses.second: and look upon the face of your Anointed.

verses.first: For one day in your courts is better than a thousand in my own room,
verses.second: and to stand at the threshold of the house of my God than to dwell in the tents of the wicked.

verses.first: For the Lord God is both sun and shield;
verses.second: he will give grace and glory;

verses.first: No good thing will the Lord withhold
verses.second: from those who walk with integrity.

verses.first: O Lord of hosts,
verses.second: happy are they who put their trust in you!

verses.first: You have been gracious to your land, O Lord,
verses.second: you have restored the good fortune of Jacob.

verses.first: You have forgiven the iniquity of your people
verses.second: and blotted out all their sins.

verses.first: You have withdrawn all your fury
verses.second: and turned yourself from your wrathful indignation.

verses.first: Restore us then, O God our Savior;
verses.second: let your anger depart from us.

verses.first: Will you be displeased with us for ever?
verses.second: will you prolong your anger from age to age?

verses.first: Will you not give us life again,
verses.second: that your people may rejoice in you?

verses.first: Show us your mercy, O Lord,
verses.second: and grant us your salvation.

verses.first: I will listen to what the Lord God is saying,
verses.second: for he is speaking peace to his faithful people and to those who turn their hearts to him.

verses.first: Truly, his salvation is very near to those who fear him,
verses.second: that his glory may dwell in our land.

verses.first: Mercy and truth have met together;
verses.second: righteousness and peace have kissed each other.

verses.first: Truth shall spring up from the earth,
verses.second: and righteousness shall look down from heaven.

verses.first: The Lord will indeed grant prosperity,
verses.second: and our land will yield its increase.

verses.first: Righteousness shall go before him,
verses.second: and peace shall be a pathway for his feet.

verses.first: Bow down your ear, O Lord, and answer me,
verses.second: for I am poor and in misery.

verses.first: Keep watch over my life, for I am faithful;
verses.second: save your servant who puts his trust in you.

verses.first: Be merciful to me, O Lord, for you are my God;
verses.second: I call upon you all the day long.

verses.first: Gladden the soul of your servant,
verses.second: for to you, O Lord, I lift up my soul.

verses.first: For you, O Lord, are good and forgiving,
verses.second: and great is your love toward all who call upon you.

verses.first: Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer,
verses.second: and attend to the voice of my supplications.

verses.first: In the time of my trouble I will call upon you,
verses.second: for you will answer me.

verses.first: Among the gods there is none like you, O Lord,
verses.second: nor anything like your works.

verses.first: All nations you have made will come and worship you, O Lord,
verses.second: and glorify your Name.

verses.first: For you are great; you do wondrous things;
verses.second: and you alone are God.

verses.first: Teach me your way, O Lord, and I will walk in your truth;
verses.second: knit my heart to you that I may fear your Name.

verses.first: I will thank you, O Lord my God, with all my heart,
verses.second: and glorify your Name for evermore.

verses.first: For great is your love toward me;
verses.second: you have delivered me from the nethermost Pit.

verses.first: The arrogant rise up against me, O God, and a band of violent men seeks my life;
verses.second: they have not set you before their eyes.

verses.first: But you, O Lord, are gracious and full of compassion,
verses.second: slow to anger, and full of kindness and truth.

verses.first: Turn to me and have mercy upon me;
verses.second: give your strength to your servant; and save the child of your handmaid.

verses.first: Show me a sign of your favor, so that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed;
verses.second: because you, O Lord, have helped me and comforted me.

verses.first: On the holy mountain stands the city he has founded;
verses.second: the Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.

verses.first: Glorious things are spoken of you,
verses.second: O city of our God.

verses.first: I count Egypt and Babylon among those who know me;
verses.second: behold Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia: in Zion were they born.

verses.first: Of Zion it shall be said, “Everyone was born in her,
verses.second: and the Most High himself shall sustain her.”

verses.first: The Lord will record as he enrolls the peoples,
verses.second: “These also were born there.”

verses.first: The singers and the dancers will say,
verses.second: “All my fresh springs are in you.”

verses.first: O Lord, my God, my Savior,
verses.second: by day and night I cry to you.

verses.first: Let my prayer enter into your presence;
verses.second: incline your ear to my lamentation.

verses.first: For I am full of trouble;
verses.second: my life is at the brink of the grave.

verses.first: I am counted among those who go down to the Pit;
verses.second: I have become like one who has no strength;

verses.first: Lost among the dead,
verses.second: like the slain who lie in the grave,

verses.first: Whom you remember no more,
verses.second: for they are cut off from your hand.

verses.first: You have laid me in the depths of the Pit,
verses.second: in dark places, and in the abyss.

verses.first: Your anger weighs upon me heavily,
verses.second: and all your great waves overwhelm me.

verses.first: You have put my friends far from me; you have made me to be abhorred by them;
verses.second: I am in prison and cannot get free.

verses.first: My sight has failed me because of trouble;
verses.second: Lord, I have called upon you daily; I have stretched out my hands to you.

verses.first: Do you work wonders for the dead?
verses.second: will those who have died stand up and give you thanks?

verses.first: Will your loving-kindness be declared in the grave?
verses.second: your faithfulness in the land of destruction?

verses.first: Will your wonders be known in the dark?
verses.second: or your righteousness in the country where all is forgotten?

verses.first: But as for me, O Lord, I cry to you for help;
verses.second: in the morning my prayer comes before you. `

verses.first: Lord, why have you rejected me?
verses.second: why have you hidden your face from me?

verses.first: Ever since my youth, I have been wretched and at the point of death;
verses.second: I have borne your terrors with a troubled mind.

verses.first: Your blazing anger has swept over me;
verses.second: your terrors have destroyed me;

verses.first: They surround me all day long like a flood;
verses.second: they encompass me on every side.

verses.first: My friend and my neighbor you have put away from me,
verses.second: and darkness is my only companion.

verses.first: Your love, O Lord, for ever will I sing;
verses.second: from age to age my mouth will proclaim your faithfulness.

verses.first: For I am persuaded that your love is established for ever;
verses.second: you have set your faithfulness firmly in the heavens.

verses.first: “I have made a covenant with my chosen one;
verses.second: I have sworn an oath to David my servant:

verses.first: ‘I will establish your line for ever,
verses.second: and preserve your throne for all generations.’”

verses.first: The heavens bear witness to your wonders, O Lord,
verses.second: and to your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones;

verses.first: For who in the skies can be compared to the Lord?
verses.second: who is like the Lord among the gods?

verses.first: God is much to be feared in the council of the holy ones,
verses.second: great and terrible to all those round about him.

verses.first: Who is like you, Lord God of hosts?
verses.second: O mighty Lord, your faithfulness is all around you.

verses.first: You rule the raging of the sea
verses.second: and still the surging of its waves.

verses.first: You have crushed Rahab of the deep with a deadly wound;
verses.second: you have scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.

verses.first: Yours are the heavens; the earth also is yours;
verses.second: you laid the foundations of the world and all that is in it.

verses.first: You have made the north and the south;
verses.second: Tabor and Hermon rejoice in your Name.

verses.first: You have a mighty arm;
verses.second: strong is your hand and high is your right hand.

verses.first: Righteousness and justice are the foundations of your throne;
verses.second: love and truth go before your face.

verses.first: Happy are the people who know the festal shout!
verses.second: they walk, O Lord, in the light of your presence.

verses.first: They rejoice daily in your Name;
verses.second: they are jubilant in your righteousness.

verses.first: For you are the glory of their strength,
verses.second: and by your favor our might is exalted.

verses.first: Truly, the Lord is our ruler;
verses.second: the Holy One of Israel is our King.

verses.first: You spoke once in a vision and said to your faithful people:
verses.second: “I have set the crown upon a warrior and have exalted one chosen out of the people.

verses.first: I have found David my servant;
verses.second: with my holy oil have I anointed him.

verses.first: My hand will hold him fast
verses.second: and my arm will make him strong.

verses.first: No enemy shall deceive him,
verses.second: nor any wicked man bring him down.

verses.first: I will crush his foes before him
verses.second: and strike down those who hate him.

verses.first: My faithfulness and love shall be with him,
verses.second: and he shall be victorious through my Name.

verses.first: I shall make his dominion extend
verses.second: from the Great Sea to the River.

verses.first: He will say to me, ‘You are my Father,
verses.second: my God, and the rock of my salvation.’

verses.first: I will make him my firstborn
verses.second: and higher than the kings of the earth.

verses.first: I will keep my love for him for ever,
verses.second: and my covenant will stand firm for him.

verses.first: I will establish his line for ever
verses.second: and his throne as the days of heaven.”

verses.first: “If his children forsake my law
verses.second: and do not walk according to my judgments;

verses.first: If they break my statutes
verses.second: and do not keep my commandments;

verses.first: I will punish their transgressions with a rod
verses.second: and their iniquities with the lash;

verses.first: But I will not take my love from him,
verses.second: nor let my faithfulness prove false.

verses.first: I will not break my covenant,
verses.second: nor change what has gone out of my lips.

verses.first: Once for all I have sworn by my holiness:
verses.second: ‘I will not lie to David.

verses.first: His line shall endure for ever
verses.second: and his throne as the sun before me;

verses.first: It shall stand fast for evermore like the moon,
verses.second: the abiding witness in the sky.’”

verses.first: But you have cast off and rejected your anointed;
verses.second: you have become enraged at him.

verses.first: You have broken your covenant with your servant,
verses.second: defiled his crown, and hurled it to the ground.

verses.first: You have breached all his walls
verses.second: and laid his strongholds in ruins.

verses.first: All who pass by despoil him;
verses.second: he has become the scorn of his neighbors.

verses.first: You have exalted the right hand of his foes
verses.second: and made all his enemies rejoice.

verses.first: You have turned back the edge of his sword
verses.second: and have not sustained him in battle.

verses.first: You have put an end to his splendor
verses.second: and cast his throne to the ground.

verses.first: You have cut short the days of his youth
verses.second: and have covered him with shame.

verses.first: How long will you hide yourself, O Lord? will you hide yourself for ever?
verses.second: how long will your anger burn like fire?

verses.first: Remember, Lord, how short life is,
verses.second: how frail you have made all flesh.

verses.first: Who can live and not see death?
verses.second: who can save himself from the power of the grave?

verses.first: Where, Lord, are your loving-kindnesses of old,
verses.second: which you promised David in your faithfulness?

verses.first: Remember, Lord, how your servant is mocked,
verses.second: how I carry in my bosom the taunts of many peoples,

verses.first: The taunts your enemies have hurled, O Lord,
verses.second: which they hurled at the heels of your anointed.

verses.first: Blessed be the Lord for evermore!
verses.second: Amen, I say, Amen. Book Four

verses.first: Lord, you have been our refuge
verses.second: from one generation to another.

verses.first: Before the mountains were brought forth, or the land and the earth were born,
verses.second: from age to age you are God.

verses.first: You turn us back to the dust and say,
verses.second: “Go back, O child of earth.”

verses.first: For a thousand years in your sight are like yesterday when it is past
verses.second: and like a watch in the night.

verses.first: You sweep us away like a dream;
verses.second: we fade away suddenly like the grass.

verses.first: In the morning it is green and flourishes;
verses.second: in the evening it is dried up and withered.

verses.first: For we consume away in your displeasure;
verses.second: we are afraid because of your wrathful indignation.

verses.first: Our iniquities you have set before you,
verses.second: and our secret sins in the light of your countenance.

verses.first: When you are angry, all our days are gone;
verses.second: we bring our years to an end like a sigh.

verses.first: The span of our life is seventy years, perhaps in strength even eighty;
verses.second: yet the sum of them is but labor and sorrow, for they pass away quickly and we are gone.

verses.first: Who regards the power of your wrath?
verses.second: who rightly fears your indignation?

verses.first: So teach us to number our days
verses.second: that we may apply our hearts to wisdom.

verses.first: Return, O Lord; how long will you tarry?
verses.second: be gracious to your servants.

verses.first: Satisfy us by your loving-kindness in the morning;
verses.second: so shall we rejoice and be glad all the days of our life.

verses.first: Make us glad by the measure of the days that you afflicted us
verses.second: and the years in which we suffered adversity.

verses.first: Show your servants your works
verses.second: and your splendor to their children.

verses.first: May the graciousness of the Lord our God be upon us;
verses.second: prosper the work of our hands; prosper our handiwork.

verses.first: He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High,
verses.second: abides under the shadow of the Almighty.

verses.first: He shall say to the Lord, “You are my refuge and my stronghold,
verses.second: my God in whom I put my trust.”

verses.first: He shall deliver you from the snare of the hunter
verses.second: and from the deadly pestilence.

verses.first: He shall cover you with his pinions, and you shall find refuge under his wings;
verses.second: his faithfulness shall be a shield and buckler.

verses.first: You shall not be afraid of any terror by night,
verses.second: nor of the arrow that flies by day;

verses.first: Of the plague that stalks in the darkness,
verses.second: nor of the sickness that lays waste at mid-day.

verses.first: A thousand shall fall at your side and ten thousand at your right hand,
verses.second: but it shall not come near you.

verses.first: Your eyes have only to behold
verses.second: to see the reward of the wicked.

verses.first: Because you have made the Lord your refuge,
verses.second: and the Most High your habitation,

verses.first: There shall no evil happen to you,
verses.second: neither shall any plague come near your dwelling.

verses.first: For he shall give his angels charge over you,
verses.second: to keep you in all your ways.

verses.first: They shall bear you in their hands,
verses.second: lest you dash your foot against a stone.

verses.first: You shall tread upon the lion and adder;
verses.second: you shall trample the young lion and the serpent under your feet.

verses.first: Because he is bound to me in love, therefore will I deliver him;
verses.second: I will protect him, because he knows my Name.

verses.first: He shall call upon me, and I will answer him;
verses.second: I am with him in trouble; I will rescue him and bring him to honor.

verses.first: With long life will I satisfy him,
verses.second: and show him my salvation.

verses.first: It is a good thing to give thanks to the Lord,
verses.second: and to sing praises to your Name, O Most High;

verses.first: To tell of your loving-kindness early in the morning
verses.second: and of your faithfulness in the night season;

verses.first: On the psaltery, and on the lyre,
verses.second: and to the melody of the harp.

verses.first: For you have made me glad by your acts, O Lord;
verses.second: and I shout for joy because of the works of your hands.

verses.first: Lord, how great are your works!
verses.second: your thoughts are very deep.

verses.first: The dullard does not know, nor does the fool understand,
verses.second: that though the wicked grow like weeds, and all the workers of iniquity flourish,

verses.first: They flourish only to be destroyed for ever;
verses.second: but you, O Lord, are exalted for evermore.

verses.first: For lo, your enemies, O Lord, lo, your enemies shall perish,
verses.second: and all the workers of iniquity shall be scattered.

verses.first: But my horn you have exalted like the horns of wild bulls;
verses.second: I am anointed with fresh oil.

verses.first: My eyes also gloat over my enemies,
verses.second: and my ears rejoice to hear the doom of the wicked who rise up against me.

verses.first: The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree,
verses.second: and shall spread abroad like a cedar of Lebanon.

verses.first: Those who are planted in the house of the Lord
verses.second: shall flourish in the courts of our God;

verses.first: They shall still bear fruit in old age;
verses.second: they shall be green and succulent;

verses.first: That they may show how upright the Lord is,
verses.second: my Rock, in whom there is no fault.

verses.first: The Lord is King; he has put on splendid apparel;
verses.second: the Lord has put on his apparel and girded himself with strength.

verses.first: He has made the whole world so sure
verses.second: that it cannot be moved;

verses.first: Ever since the world began, your throne has been established;
verses.second: you are from everlasting.

verses.first: The waters have lifted up, O Lord, the waters have lifted up their voice;
verses.second: the waters have lifted up their pounding waves.

verses.first: Mightier than the sound of many waters, mightier than the breakers of the sea,
verses.second: mightier is the Lord who dwells on high.

verses.first: Your testimonies are very sure,
verses.second: and holiness adorns your house, O Lord, for ever and for evermore.

verses.first: O Lord God of vengeance,
verses.second: O God of vengeance, show yourself

verses.first: Rise up, O Judge of the world;
verses.second: give the arrogant their just deserts.

verses.first: How long shall the wicked, O Lord,
verses.second: how long shall the wicked triumph?

verses.first: They bluster in their insolence;
verses.second: all evildoers are full of boasting.

verses.first: They crush your people, O Lord,
verses.second: and afflict your chosen nation.

verses.first: They murder the widow and the stranger
verses.second: and put the orphans to death.

verses.first: Yet they say, “The Lord does not see,
verses.second: the God of Jacob takes no notice.”

verses.first: Consider well, you dullards among the people;
verses.second: when will you fools understand?

verses.first: He that planted the ear, does he not hear?
verses.second: he that formed the eye, does he not see?

verses.first: He who admonishes the nations, will he not punish?
verses.second: he who teaches all the world, has he no knowledge?

verses.first: The Lord knows our human thoughts;
verses.second: how like a puff of wind they are.

verses.first: Happy are they whom you instruct, O Lord!
verses.second: whom you teach out of your law;

verses.first: To give them rest in evil days,
verses.second: until a pit is dug for the wicked.

verses.first: For the Lord will not abandon his people,
verses.second: nor will he forsake his own.

verses.first: For judgment will again be just,
verses.second: and all the true of heart will follow it.

verses.first: Who rose up for me against the wicked?
verses.second: who took my part against the evildoers?

verses.first: If the Lord had not come to my help,
verses.second: I should soon have dwelt in the land of silence.

verses.first: As often as I said, “My foot has slipped,”
verses.second: your love, O Lord, upheld me.

verses.first: When many cares fill my mind,
verses.second: your consolations cheer my soul.

verses.first: Can a corrupt tribunal have any part with you,
verses.second: one which frames evil into law?

verses.first: They conspire against the life of the just
verses.second: and condemn the innocent to death.

verses.first: But the Lord has become my stronghold,
verses.second: and my God the rock of my trust.

verses.first: He will turn their wickedness back upon them and destroy them in their own malice;
verses.second: the Lord our God will destroy them.

verses.first: Come, let us sing to the Lord;
verses.second: let us shout for joy to the Rock of our salvation.

verses.first: Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving
verses.second: and raise a loud shout to him with psalms.

verses.first: For the Lord is a great God,
verses.second: and a great King above all gods.

verses.first: In his hand are the caverns of the earth,
verses.second: and the heights of the hills are his also.

verses.first: The sea is his, for he made it,
verses.second: and his hands have molded the dry land.

verses.first: Come, let us bow down, and bend the knee,
verses.second: and kneel before the Lord our Maker.

verses.first: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
verses.second: Oh, that today you would hearken to his voice!

verses.first: Harden not your hearts, as your forebears did in the wilderness,
verses.second: at Meribah, and on that day at Massah, when they tempted me.

verses.first: They put me to the test,
verses.second: though they had seen my works.

verses.first: Forty years long I detested that generation and said,
verses.second: “This people are wayward in their hearts; they do not know my ways.”

verses.first: So I swore in my wrath,
verses.second: “They shall not enter into my rest.”

verses.first: Sing to the Lord a new song;
verses.second: sing to the Lord, all the whole earth.

verses.first: Sing to the Lord and bless his Name;
verses.second: proclaim the good news of his salvation from day to day.

verses.first: Declare his glory among the nations
verses.second: and his wonders among all peoples.

verses.first: For great is the Lord and greatly to be praised;
verses.second: he is more to be feared than all gods.

verses.first: As for all the gods of the nations, they are but idols;
verses.second: but it is the Lord who made the heavens.

verses.first: Oh, the majesty and magnificence of his presence!
verses.second: Oh, the power and the splendor of his sanctuary!

verses.first: Ascribe to the Lord, you families of the peoples;
verses.second: ascribe to the Lord honor and power.

verses.first: Ascribe to the Lord the honor due his Name;
verses.second: bring offerings and come into his courts.

verses.first: Worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness;
verses.second: let the whole earth tremble before him.

verses.first: Tell it out among the nations: “The Lord is King!
verses.second: he has made the world so firm that it cannot be moved; he will judge the peoples with equity.”

verses.first: Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad; let the sea thunder and all that is in it;
verses.second: let the field be joyful and all that is therein.

verses.first: Then shall all the trees of the wood shout for joy before the Lord when he comes,
verses.second: when he comes to judge the earth.

verses.first: He will judge the world with righteousness
verses.second: and the peoples with his truth.

verses.first: The Lord is King; let the earth rejoice;
verses.second: let the multitude of the isles be glad.

verses.first: Clouds and darkness are round about him,
verses.second: righteousness and justice are the foundations of his throne.

verses.first: A fire goes before him
verses.second: and burns up his enemies on every side.

verses.first: His lightnings light up the world;
verses.second: the earth sees it and is afraid.

verses.first: The mountains melt like wax at the presence of the Lord,
verses.second: at the presence of the Lord of the whole earth.

verses.first: The heavens declare his righteousness,
verses.second: and all the peoples see his glory.

verses.first: Confounded be all who worship carved images and delight in false gods!
verses.second: Bow down before him, all you gods.

verses.first: Zion hears and is glad, and the cities of Judah rejoice,
verses.second: because of your judgments, O Lord.

verses.first: For you are the Lord, most high over all the earth;
verses.second: you are exalted far above all gods.

verses.first: The Lord loves those who hate evil;
verses.second: he preserves the lives of his saints and delivers them from the hand of the wicked.

verses.first: Light has sprung up for the righteous,
verses.second: and joyful gladness for those who are truehearted.

verses.first: Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous,
verses.second: and give thanks to his holy Name.

verses.first: Sing to the Lord a new song,
verses.second: for he has done marvelous things.

verses.first: With his right hand and his holy arm
verses.second: has he won for himself the victory.

verses.first: The Lord has made known his victory;
verses.second: his righteousness has he openly shown in the sight of the nations.

verses.first: He remembers his mercy and faithfulness to the house of Israel,
verses.second: and all the ends of the earth have seen the victory of our God.

verses.first: Shout with joy to the Lord, all you lands;
verses.second: lift up your voice, rejoice, and sing.

verses.first: Sing to the Lord with the harp,
verses.second: with the harp and the voice of song.

verses.first: With trumpets and the sound of the horn
verses.second: shout with joy before the King, the Lord.

verses.first: Let the sea make a noise and all that is in it,
verses.second: the lands and those who dwell therein.

verses.first: Let the rivers clap their hands,
verses.second: and let the hills ring out with joy before the Lord, when he comes to judge the earth.

verses.first: In righteousness shall he judge the world
verses.second: and the peoples with equity.

verses.first: The Lord is King; let the people tremble;
verses.second: he is enthroned upon the cherubim; let the earth shake.

verses.first: The Lord is great in Zion;
verses.second: he is high above all peoples.

verses.first: Let them confess his Name, which is great and awesome;
verses.second: he is the Holy One.

verses.first: “O mighty King, lover of justice, you have established equity;
verses.second: you have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob.”

verses.first: Proclaim the greatness of the Lord our God and fall down before his footstool;
verses.second: he is the Holy One.

verses.first: Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among those who call upon his Name,
verses.second: they called upon the Lord, and he answered them.

verses.first: He spoke to them out of the pillar of cloud;
verses.second: they kept his testimonies and the decree that he gave them.

verses.first: “O Lord our God, you answered them indeed;
verses.second: you were a God who forgave them, yet punished them for their evil deeds.”

verses.first: Proclaim the greatness of the Lord our God and worship him upon his holy hill;
verses.second: for the Lord our God is the Holy One.

verses.first: Be joyful in the Lord, all you lands;
verses.second: serve the Lord with gladness and come before his presence with a song.

verses.first: Know this: The Lord himself is God;
verses.second: he himself has made us, and we are his; we are his people and the sheep of his pasture.

verses.first: Enter his gates with thanksgiving; go into his courts with praise;
verses.second: give thanks to him and call upon his Name.

verses.first: For the Lord is good; his mercy is everlasting;
verses.second: and his faithfulness endures from age to age.

verses.first: I will sing of mercy and justice;
verses.second: to you, O Lord, will I sing praises.

verses.first: I will strive to follow a blameless course; oh, when will you come to me?
verses.second: I will walk with sincerity of heart within my house.

verses.first: I will set no worthless thing before my eyes;
verses.second: I hate the doers of evil deeds; they shall not remain with me.

verses.first: A crooked heart shall be far from me;
verses.second: I will not know evil.

verses.first: Those who in secret slander their neighbors I will destroy;
verses.second: those who have a haughty look and a proud heart I cannot abide.

verses.first: My eyes are upon the faithful in the land, that they may dwell with me,
verses.second: and only those who lead a blameless life shall be my servants.

verses.first: Those who act deceitfully shall not dwell in my house,
verses.second: and those who tell lies shall not continue in my sight.

verses.first: I will soon destroy all the wicked in the land,
verses.second: that I may root out all evildoers from the city of the Lord.

verses.first: Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come before you;
verses.second: hide not your face from me in the day of my trouble.

verses.first: Incline your ear to me;
verses.second: when I call, make haste to answer me,

verses.first: For my days drift away like smoke,
verses.second: and my bones are hot as burning coals.

verses.first: My heart is smitten like grass and withered,
verses.second: so that I forget to eat my bread.

verses.first: Because of the voice of my groaning
verses.second: I am but skin and bones.

verses.first: I have become like a vulture in the wilderness,
verses.second: like an owl among the ruins.

verses.first: I lie awake and groan;
verses.second: I am like a sparrow, lonely on a house-top.

verses.first: My enemies revile me all day long,
verses.second: and those who scoff at me have taken an oath against me.

verses.first: For I have eaten ashes for bread
verses.second: and mingled my drink with weeping.

verses.first: Because of your indignation and wrath
verses.second: you have lifted me up and thrown me away.

verses.first: My days pass away like a shadow,
verses.second: and I wither like the grass.

verses.first: But you, O Lord, endure for ever,
verses.second: and your Name from age to age.

verses.first: You will arise and have compassion on Zion, for it is time to have mercy upon her;
verses.second: indeed, the appointed time has come.

verses.first: For your servants love her very rubble,
verses.second: and are moved to pity even for her dust.

verses.first: The nations shall fear your Name, O Lord,
verses.second: and all the kings of the earth your glory.

verses.first: For the Lord will build up Zion,
verses.second: and his glory will appear.

verses.first: He will look with favor on the prayer of the homeless;
verses.second: he will not despise their plea.

verses.first: Let this be written for a future generation,
verses.second: so that a people yet unborn may praise the Lord.

verses.first: For the Lord looked down from his holy place on high;
verses.second: from the heavens he beheld the earth;

verses.first: That he might hear the groan of the captive
verses.second: and set free those condemned to die;

verses.first: That they may declare in Zion the Name of the Lord,
verses.second: and his praise in Jerusalem;

verses.first: When the peoples are gathered together,
verses.second: and the kingdoms also, to serve the Lord.

verses.first: He has brought down my strength before my time;
verses.second: he has shortened the number of my days;

verses.first: And I said, “O my God, do not take me away in the midst of my days;
verses.second: your years endure throughout all generations.

verses.first: In the beginning, O Lord, you laid the foundations of the earth,
verses.second: and the heavens are the work of your hands;

verses.first: They shall perish, but you will endure; they all shall wear out like a garment;
verses.second: as clothing you will change them, and they shall be changed;

verses.first: But you are always the same,
verses.second: and your years will never end.

verses.first: The children of your servants shall continue,
verses.second: and their offspring shall stand fast in your sight.”

verses.first: Bless the Lord, O my soul,
verses.second: and all that is within me, bless his holy Name.

verses.first: Bless the Lord, O my soul,
verses.second: and forget not all his benefits.

verses.first: He forgives all your sins
verses.second: and heals all your infirmities;

verses.first: He redeems your life from the grave
verses.second: and crowns you with mercy and loving-kindness;

verses.first: He satisfies you with good things,
verses.second: and your youth is renewed like an eagle’s.

verses.first: The Lord executes righteousness
verses.second: and judgment for all who are oppressed.

verses.first: He made his ways known to Moses
verses.second: and his works to the children of Israel.

verses.first: The Lord is full of compassion and mercy,
verses.second: slow to anger and of great kindness.

verses.first: He will not always accuse us,
verses.second: nor will he keep his anger for ever.

verses.first: He has not dealt with us according to our sins,
verses.second: nor rewarded us according to our wickedness.

verses.first: For as the heavens are high above the earth,
verses.second: so is his mercy great upon those who fear him.

verses.first: As far as the east is from the west,
verses.second: so far has he removed our sins from us.

verses.first: As a father cares for his children,
verses.second: so does the Lord care for those who fear him.

verses.first: For he himself knows whereof we are made;
verses.second: he remembers that we are but dust.

verses.first: Our days are like the grass;
verses.second: we flourish like a flower of the field;

verses.first: When the wind goes over it, it is gone,
verses.second: and its place shall know it no more.

verses.first: But the merciful goodness of the Lord endures for ever on those who fear him,
verses.second: and his righteousness on children’s children;

verses.first: On those who keep his covenant
verses.second: and remember his commandments and do them.

verses.first: The Lord has set his throne in heaven,
verses.second: and his kingship has dominion over all.

verses.first: Bless the Lord, you angels of his, you mighty ones who do his bidding,
verses.second: and hearken to the voice of his word.

verses.first: Bless the Lord, all you his hosts,
verses.second: you ministers of his who do his will.

verses.first: Bless the Lord, all you works of his, in all places of his dominion;
verses.second: bless the Lord, O my soul.

verses.first: Bless the Lord, O my soul;
verses.second: O Lord my God, how excellent is your greatness! you are clothed with majesty and splendor.

verses.first: You wrap yourself with light as with a cloak
verses.second: and spread out the heavens like a curtain.

verses.first: You lay the beams of your chambers in the waters above;
verses.second: you make the clouds your chariot; you ride on the wings of the wind.

verses.first: You make the winds your messengers
verses.second: and flames of fire your servants.

verses.first: You have set the earth upon its foundations,
verses.second: so that it never shall move at any time.

verses.first: You covered it with the Deep as with a mantle;
verses.second: the waters stood higher than the mountains.

verses.first: At your rebuke they fled;
verses.second: at the voice of your thunder they hastened away.

verses.first: They went up into the hills and down to the valleys beneath,
verses.second: to the places you had appointed for them.

verses.first: You set the limits that they should not pass;
verses.second: they shall not again cover the earth.

verses.first: You send the springs into the valleys;
verses.second: they flow between the mountains.

verses.first: All the beasts of the field drink their fill from them,
verses.second: and the wild asses quench their thirst.

verses.first: Beside them the birds of the air make their nests
verses.second: and sing among the branches.

verses.first: You water the mountains from your dwelling on high;
verses.second: the earth is fully satisfied by the fruit of your works.

verses.first: You make grass grow for flocks and herds
verses.second: and plants to serve mankind;

verses.first: That they may bring forth food from the earth,
verses.second: and wine to gladden our hearts,

verses.first: Oil to make a cheerful countenance,
verses.second: and bread to strengthen the heart.

verses.first: The trees of the Lord are full of sap,
verses.second: the cedars of Lebanon which he planted,

verses.first: In which the birds build their nests,
verses.second: and in whose tops the stork makes his dwelling.

verses.first: The high hills are a refuge for the mountain goats,
verses.second: and the stony cliffs for the rock badgers.

verses.first: You appointed the moon to mark the seasons,
verses.second: and the sun knows the time of its setting.

verses.first: You make darkness that it may be night,
verses.second: in which all the beasts of the forest prowl.

verses.first: The lions roar after their prey
verses.second: and seek their food from God.

verses.first: The sun rises, and they slip away
verses.second: and lay themselves down in their dens.

verses.first: Man goes forth to his work
verses.second: and to his labor until the evening.

verses.first: O Lord, how manifold are your works!
verses.second: in wisdom you have made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.

verses.first: Yonder is the great and wide sea with its living things too many to number,
verses.second: creatures both small and great.

verses.first: There move the ships, and there is that Leviathan,
verses.second: which you have made for the sport of it.

verses.first: All of them look to you
verses.second: to give them their food in due season.

verses.first: You give it to them; they gather it;
verses.second: you open your hand, and they are filled with good things.

verses.first: You hide your face, and they are terrified;
verses.second: you take away their breath, and they die and return to their dust.

verses.first: You send forth your Spirit, and they are created;
verses.second: and so you renew the face of the earth.

verses.first: May the glory of the Lord endure for ever;
verses.second: may the Lord rejoice in all his works.

verses.first: He looks at the earth and it trembles;
verses.second: he touches the mountains and they smoke.

verses.first: I will sing to the Lord as long as I live;
verses.second: I will praise my God while I have my being.

verses.first: May these words of mine please him;
verses.second: I will rejoice in the Lord.

verses.first: Let sinners be consumed out of the earth,
verses.second: and the wicked be no more.

verses.first: Bless the Lord, O my soul.
verses.second: Hallelujah!

verses.first: Give thanks to the Lord and call upon his Name;
verses.second: make known his deeds among the peoples.

verses.first: Sing to him, sing praises to him,
verses.second: and speak of all his marvelous works.

verses.first: Glory in his holy Name;
verses.second: let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice.

verses.first: Search for the Lord and his strength;
verses.second: continually seek his face.

verses.first: Remember the marvels he has done,
verses.second: his wonders and the judgments of his mouth,

verses.first: O offspring of Abraham his servant,
verses.second: O children of Jacob his chosen.

verses.first: He is the Lord our God;
verses.second: his judgments prevail in all the world.

verses.first: He has always been mindful of his covenant,
verses.second: the promise he made for a thousand generations:

verses.first: The covenant he made with Abraham,
verses.second: the oath that he swore to Isaac,

verses.first: Which he established as a statute for Jacob,
verses.second: an everlasting covenant for Israel,

verses.first: Saying, “To you will I give the land of Canaan
verses.second: to be your allotted inheritance.”

verses.first: When they were few in number,
verses.second: of little account, and sojourners in the land,

verses.first: Wandering from nation to nation
verses.second: and from one kingdom to another,

verses.first: He let no one oppress them
verses.second: and rebuked kings for their sake,

verses.first: Saying, “Do not touch my anointed
verses.second: and do my prophets no harm.”

verses.first: Then he called for a famine in the land
verses.second: and destroyed the supply of bread.

verses.first: He sent a man before them,
verses.second: Joseph, who was sold as a slave.

verses.first: They bruised his feet in fetters;
verses.second: his neck they put in an iron collar.

verses.first: Until his prediction came to pass,
verses.second: the word of the Lord tested him.

verses.first: The king sent and released him;
verses.second: the ruler of the peoples set him free.

verses.first: He set him as a master over his household,
verses.second: as a ruler over all his possessions,

verses.first: To instruct his princes according to his will
verses.second: and to teach his elders wisdom.

verses.first: Israel came into Egypt,
verses.second: and Jacob became a sojourner in the land of Ham.

verses.first: The Lord made his people exceedingly fruitful;
verses.second: he made them stronger than their enemies;

verses.first: Whose heart he turned, so that they hated his people,
verses.second: and dealt unjustly with his servants.

verses.first: He sent Moses his servant,
verses.second: and Aaron whom he had chosen.

verses.first: They worked his signs among them,
verses.second: and portents in the land of Ham.

verses.first: He sent darkness, and it grew dark;
verses.second: but the Egyptians rebelled against his words.

verses.first: He turned their waters into blood
verses.second: and caused their fish to die.

verses.first: Their land was overrun by frogs,
verses.second: in the very chambers of their kings.

verses.first: He spoke, and there came swarms of insects
verses.second: and gnats within all their borders.

verses.first: He gave them hailstones instead of rain,
verses.second: and flames of fire throughout their land.

verses.first: He blasted their vines and their fig trees
verses.second: and shattered every tree in their country.

verses.first: He spoke, and the locust came,
verses.second: and young locusts without number,

verses.first: Which ate up all the green plants in their land
verses.second: and devoured the fruit of their soil.

verses.first: He struck down the firstborn of their land,
verses.second: the first fruits of all their strength.

verses.first: He led out his people with silver and gold;
verses.second: in all their tribes there was not one that stumbled.

verses.first: Egypt was glad of their going,
verses.second: because they were afraid of them.

verses.first: He spread out a cloud for a covering
verses.second: and a fire to give light in the night season.

verses.first: They asked, and quails appeared,
verses.second: and he satisfied them with bread from heaven.

verses.first: He opened the rock, and water flowed,
verses.second: so the river ran in the dry places.

verses.first: For God remembered his holy word
verses.second: and Abraham his servant.

verses.first: So he led forth his people with gladness,
verses.second: his chosen with shouts of joy.

verses.first: He gave his people the lands of the nations,
verses.second: and they took the fruit of others’ toil,

verses.first: That they might keep his statutes
verses.second: and observe his laws. Hallelujah!

verses.first: Hallelujah! Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good,
verses.second: for his mercy endures for ever.

verses.first: Who can declare the mighty acts of the Lord
verses.second: or show forth all his praise?

verses.first: Happy are those who act with justice
verses.second: and always do what is right!

verses.first: Remember me, O Lord, with the favor you have for your people,
verses.second: and visit me with your saving help;

verses.first: That I may see the prosperity of your elect and be glad with the gladness of your people,
verses.second: that I may glory with your inheritance.

verses.first: We have sinned as our forebears did;
verses.second: we have done wrong and dealt wickedly.

verses.first: In Egypt they did not consider your marvelous works, nor remember the abundance of your love;
verses.second: they defied the Most High at the Red Sea.

verses.first: But he saved them for his Name’s sake,
verses.second: to make his power known.

verses.first: He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up,
verses.second: and he led them through the deep as through a desert.

verses.first: He saved them from the hand of those who hated them
verses.second: and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.

verses.first: The waters covered their oppressors;
verses.second: not one of them was left.

verses.first: Then they believed his words
verses.second: and sang him songs of praise.

verses.first: But they soon forgot his deeds
verses.second: and did not wait for his counsel.

verses.first: A craving seized them in the wilderness,
verses.second: and they put God to the test in the desert.

verses.first: He gave them what they asked,
verses.second: but sent leanness into their soul.

verses.first: They envied Moses in the camp,
verses.second: and Aaron, the holy one of the Lord.

verses.first: The earth opened and swallowed Dathan
verses.second: and covered the company of Abiram.

verses.first: Fire blazed up against their company,
verses.second: and flames devoured the wicked.

verses.first: Israel made a bull-calf at Horeb
verses.second: and worshiped a molten image;

verses.first: And so they exchanged their Glory
verses.second: for the image of an ox that feeds on grass.

verses.first: They forgot God their Savior,
verses.second: who had done great things in Egypt,

verses.first: Wonderful deeds in the land of Ham,
verses.second: and fearful things at the Red Sea.

verses.first: So he would have destroyed them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach,
verses.second: to turn away his wrath from consuming them.

verses.first: They refused the pleasant land
verses.second: and would not believe his promise.

verses.first: They grumbled in their tents
verses.second: and would not listen to the voice of the Lord.

verses.first: So he lifted his hand against them,
verses.second: to overthrow them in the wilderness,

verses.first: To cast out their seed among the nations,
verses.second: and to scatter them throughout the lands.

verses.first: They joined themselves to Baal-Peor
verses.second: and ate sacrifices offered to the dead.

verses.first: They provoked him to anger with their actions,
verses.second: and a plague broke out among them.

verses.first: Then Phinehas stood up and interceded,
verses.second: and the plague came to an end.

verses.first: This was reckoned to him as righteousness
verses.second: throughout all generations for ever.

verses.first: Again they provoked his anger at the waters of Meribah,
verses.second: so that he punished Moses because of them;

verses.first: For they so embittered his spirit
verses.second: that he spoke rash words with his lips.

verses.first: They did not destroy the peoples
verses.second: as the Lord had commanded them.

verses.first: They intermingled with the heathen
verses.second: and learned their pagan ways,

verses.first: So that they worshiped their idols,
verses.second: which became a snare to them.

verses.first: They sacrificed their sons
verses.second: and their daughters to evil spirits.

verses.first: They shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters,
verses.second: which they offered to the idols of Canaan, and the land was defiled with blood.

verses.first: Thus they were polluted by their actions
verses.second: and went whoring in their evil deeds.

verses.first: Therefore the wrath of the Lord was kindled against his people
verses.second: and he abhorred his inheritance.

verses.first: He gave them over to the hand of the heathen,
verses.second: and those who hated them ruled over them.

verses.first: Their enemies oppressed them,
verses.second: and they were humbled under their hand.

verses.first: Many a time did he deliver them, but they rebelled through their own devices,
verses.second: and were brought down in their iniquity.

verses.first: Nevertheless, he saw their distress,
verses.second: when he heard their lamentation.

verses.first: He remembered his covenant with them
verses.second: and relented in accordance with his great mercy.

verses.first: He caused them to be pitied
verses.second: by those who held them captive.

verses.first: Save us, O Lord our God, and gather us from among the nations,
verses.second: that we may give thanks to your holy Name and glory in your praise.

verses.first: Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from everlasting and to everlasting;
verses.second: and let all the people say, “Amen!” Hallelujah! Book Five

verses.first: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good,
verses.second: and his mercy endures for ever.

verses.first: Let all those whom the Lord has redeemed proclaim
verses.second: that he redeemed them from the hand of the foe.

verses.first: He gathered them out of the lands;
verses.second: from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south.

verses.first: Some wandered in desert wastes;
verses.second: they found no way to a city where they might dwell.

verses.first: They were hungry and thirsty;
verses.second: their spirits languished within them.

verses.first: Then they cried to the Lord in their trouble,
verses.second: and he delivered them from their distress.

verses.first: He put their feet on a straight path
verses.second: to go to a city where they might dwell.

verses.first: Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercy
verses.second: and the wonders he does for his children.

verses.first: For he satisfies the thirsty
verses.second: and fills the hungry with good things.

verses.first: Some sat in darkness and deep gloom,
verses.second: bound fast in misery and iron;

verses.first: Because they rebelled against the words of God
verses.second: and despised the counsel of the Most High.

verses.first: So he humbled their spirits with hard labor;
verses.second: they stumbled, and there was none to help.

verses.first: Then they cried to the Lord in their trouble,
verses.second: and he delivered them from their distress.

verses.first: He led them out of darkness and deep gloom
verses.second: and broke their bonds asunder.

verses.first: Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercy
verses.second: and the wonders he does for his children.

verses.first: For he shatters the doors of bronze
verses.second: and breaks in two the iron bars.

verses.first: Some were fools and took to rebellious ways;
verses.second: they were afflicted because of their sins.

verses.first: They abhorred all manner of food
verses.second: and drew near to death’s door.

verses.first: Then they cried to the Lord in their trouble,
verses.second: and he delivered them from their distress.

verses.first: He sent forth his word and healed them
verses.second: and saved them from the grave.

verses.first: Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercy
verses.second: and the wonders he does for his children.

verses.first: Let them offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving
verses.second: and tell of his acts with shouts of joy.

verses.first: Some went down to the sea in ships
verses.second: and plied their trade in deep waters;

verses.first: They beheld the works of the Lord
verses.second: and his wonders in the deep.

verses.first: Then he spoke, and a stormy wind arose,
verses.second: which tossed high the waves of the sea.

verses.first: They mounted up to the heavens and fell back to the depths;
verses.second: their hearts melted because of their peril.

verses.first: They reeled and staggered like drunkards
verses.second: and were at their wits’ end.

verses.first: Then they cried to the Lord in their trouble,
verses.second: and he delivered them from their distress.

verses.first: He stilled the storm to a whisper
verses.second: and quieted the waves of the sea.

verses.first: Then were they glad because of the calm,
verses.second: and he brought them to the harbor they were bound for.

verses.first: Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercy
verses.second: and the wonders he does for his children.

verses.first: Let them exalt him in the congregation of the people
verses.second: and praise him in the council of the elders.

verses.first: The Lord changed rivers into deserts,
verses.second: and water-springs into thirsty ground,

verses.first: A fruitful land into salt flats,
verses.second: because of the wickedness of those who dwell there.

verses.first: He changed deserts into pools of water
verses.second: and dry land into water-springs.

verses.first: He settled the hungry there,
verses.second: and they founded a city to dwell in.

verses.first: They sowed fields, and planted vineyards,
verses.second: and brought in a fruitful harvest.

verses.first: He blessed them, so that they increased greatly;
verses.second: he did not let their herds decrease.

verses.first: Yet when they were diminished and brought low,
verses.second: through stress of adversity and sorrow,

verses.first: (He pours contempt on princes
verses.second: and makes them wander in trackless wastes)

verses.first: He lifted up the poor out of misery
verses.second: and multiplied their families like flocks of sheep.

verses.first: The upright will see this and rejoice,
verses.second: but all wickedness will shut its mouth.

verses.first: Whoever is wise will ponder these things,
verses.second: and consider well the mercies of the Lord.

verses.first: My heart is firmly fixed, O God, my heart is fixed;
verses.second: I will sing and make melody.

verses.first: Wake up, my spirit; awake, lute and harp;
verses.second: I myself will waken the dawn.

verses.first: I will confess you among the peoples, O Lord;
verses.second: I will sing praises to you among the nations.

verses.first: For your loving-kindness is greater than the heavens,
verses.second: and your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.

verses.first: Exalt yourself above the heavens, O God,
verses.second: and your glory over all the earth.

verses.first: So that those who are dear to you may be delivered,
verses.second: save with your right hand and answer me.

verses.first: God spoke from his holy place and said,
verses.second: “I will exult and parcel out Shechem; I will divide the valley of Succoth.

verses.first: Gilead is mine and Manasseh is mine;
verses.second: Ephraim is my helmet and Judah my scepter.

verses.first: Moab is my washbasin, on Edom I throw down my sandal to claim it,
verses.second: and over Philistia will I shout in triumph.”

verses.first: Who will lead me into the strong city?
verses.second: who will bring me into Edom?

verses.first: Have you not cast us off, O God?
verses.second: you no longer go out, O God, with our armies.

verses.first: Grant us your help against the enemy,
verses.second: for vain is the help of man.

verses.first: With God we will do valiant deeds,
verses.second: and he shall tread our enemies under foot.

verses.first: Hold not your tongue, O God of my praise;
verses.second: for the mouth of the wicked, the mouth of the deceitful, is opened against me.

verses.first: They speak to me with a lying tongue;
verses.second: they encompass me with hateful words and fight against me without a cause.

verses.first: Despite my love, they accuse me;
verses.second: but as for me, I pray for them.

verses.first: They repay evil for good,
verses.second: and hatred for my love.

verses.first: Set a wicked man against him,
verses.second: and let an accuser stand at his right hand.

verses.first: When he is judged, let him be found guilty,
verses.second: and let his appeal be in vain.

verses.first: Let his days be few,
verses.second: and let another take his office.

verses.first: Let his children be fatherless,
verses.second: and his wife become a widow.

verses.first: Let his children be waifs and beggars;
verses.second: let them be driven from the ruins of their homes.

verses.first: Let the creditor seize everything he has;
verses.second: let strangers plunder his gains.

verses.first: Let there be no one to show him kindness,
verses.second: and none to pity his fatherless children.

verses.first: Let his descendants be destroyed,
verses.second: and his name be blotted out in the next generation.

verses.first: Let the wickedness of his fathers be remembered before the Lord,
verses.second: and his mother’s sin not be blotted out;

verses.first: Let their sin be always before the Lord;
verses.second: but let him root out their names from the earth;

verses.first: Because he did not remember to show mercy,
verses.second: but persecuted the poor and needy and sought to kill the brokenhearted.

verses.first: He loved cursing, let it come upon him;
verses.second: he took no delight in blessing, let it depart from him.

verses.first: He put on cursing like a garment,
